The type error is real and provable. GetTickCount() returns uint and wraps every 2^32 ms (~49.7 days of terminal uptime); t0 is declared ulong at 651, so in `(GetTickCount() - t0) < 60000` at 653 the fresh uint is zero-extended to ulong before the subtraction instead of wrapping modulo 2^32. core-engine-8.corrected: Correct, with one precision: m_clock IS restored (line 1631), so speed is not desynchronised between m_state and the clock — the speed issue is only that a per-stream speed the user has since changed is reverted and then persisted by SaveInto. reasons: The strict comparison and the coincidence it fails on are both provable. CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Truncate floors to the M1 open, CustomRatesDelete/CustomTicksDelete from that instant inclusive, and returns bar_open (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:712-744) — matching the contract text at SSR_IReplaySink.mqh:46-59 ('everything at or after from_msc must cease to exist'). Pump emits PendingRange(now) with hi == now and advances the cursor to it (1015-1017, 531) before TakeSnapshot sets taken_at_msc = m_clock.now_msc (1598), so snap.cursor.emitted_msc == snap.taken_at_msc. When taken_at is exactly an M1 open, actual == emitted and the `if(actual < m_cursor.emitted_msc)` at 1637 does not fire, so the cursor keeps claiming an instant whose tick was just deleted; the next EmitWindow's keep filter (`t < lo`, 462-464) drops the i=0 tick, whose time_msc is exactly base_msc and whose bid is bar.open (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:148-152). The bar therefore rebuilds from the second synthetic tick (base + span/(n-1) = +8571ms at 8 ticks) and its open no longer matches the broker's. Contrast is correct: SeekTo (1233) and Reset (1286) call RewindTo(actual) unconditionally. Reachability is the only soft part — it needs a checkpoint pump to land exactly on a minute boundary, which fixed-delta high-speed pumping produces (4000ms steps at 100x divide 60000 and 300000) and jittery wall deltas make rare.

The off-by-one is provable from the two contracts in source. CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Truncate (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:712-743) floors to bar_open, issues CustomRatesDelete/CustomTicksDelete from that instant inclusive, and returns bar_open; CSSRCustomSymbolSink::TruncateFrom passes it through (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:340-364). SSRReplayCursor.emitted_msc is documented as the last instant handed to the sink (SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh:25) and Pump advances it to hi == now (line 531 via PendingRange at 1015-1017) before the checkpoint is taken at 1039-1044, so snap.cursor.emitted_msc == snap.taken_at_msc. When taken_at is exactly an M1 open, actual == emitted and the strict `<` at line 1637 skips RewindTo, leaving the cursor claiming an instant whose tick the sink just deleted. The i=0 synthesised tick is stamped exactly at the bar open (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:132-147: time_msc = base_msc + i*span/(n-1)), so that is precisely the tick lost, and the rebuilt bar opens at i=1 (base + 59999/7 = +8571 ms). SeekTo (1236) and Reset (1279-1281) call RewindTo(actual) unconditionally, as the finding says. Kept at LOW: whether a checkpoint ever lands exactly on a minute boundary depends on the wall deltas fed to Pump, which is runtime, but the comparison error itself is static.

Every premise checks out. CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Truncate deletes rates and ticks from SSRBarOpenMsc(from) and returns that bar open (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:713-743); the sink contract is 'at or after' (SSR_IReplaySink.mqh:304-317); emitted_msc is 'the last instant handed to the sink' (SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh:25); Pump emits PendingRange(now) before the checkpoint is taken (controller 1015-1017 vs 1039-1044), so snap.cursor.emitted_msc == snap.taken_at_msc. When the checkpoint instant is itself an M1 open, actual == emitted and the strict `<` at line 1637 skips RewindTo, so the tick stamped exactly at that open — Synthesize writes tick i=0 at base_msc exactly (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:145-147) — is deleted and never re-emitted, since the next window starts at emitted+1 and the trim at 462-466 drops t < lo. The rebuilt candle then opens at the i=1 tick, 3/7 of the way along the first path segment (u = i*3/(n-1) with n=8). Reachability is a coincidence rather than a broker unknown: checkpoints are taken at the first pump at/after a 5-minute boundary (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:93-98) with jittery deltas (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2734-2736), so an exact-millisecond landing on a minute open is occasional, and it only matters if the user later back-steps to that checkpoint. Effect is one candle's open on the replay chart; observers are unaffected because ClipBar rebuilds the shown bar from the full synthetic array. LOW is the right ceiling. The contrast with SeekTo (1236) and Reset (1285), which call RewindTo(actual) unconditionally, is also correct.
core-engine-7.corrected: The off-by-one is real (the test should be `actual <= m_cursor.emitted_msc`, since RewindTo(actual) sets emitted = actual-1 and 'at or after actual ceased to exist'), but the simple fix collides with a second defect on the same line that the finding does not mention: SSRReplayCursor::RewindTo also zeroes tick_count and bar_count (SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh:41-47). So in the COMMON case — a mid-minute checkpoint, where actual < emitted and the branch does fire — RestoreSnapshot already discards the session counters it exists to preserve, which is the opposite of the store's stated purpose (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:5-19). The rare boundary case preserves the counters but loses the open tick. Either way RestoreSnapshot needs a rewind that re-seats emitted_msc without resetting the counters.

core-engine-11.corrected: Corrections to two sub-claims. The only money-reversing code in the class is UnwindLegsAfter (273) and that un-fill branch (664), both after the continue, so a position opened AND closed inside the deleted window keeps every balance move it made: Open() 754 (-commission), CheckPendings 356 (-commission), BookExit 222 (+realised-fee) and AccrueSwap 427 (swap). The trailing AccrueSwap() at 701 only restates positions still in m_pos, so a dropped position's swap is also stranded. The Reset path is real: SSR_GroupPort.mqh 425-437 -> CSSRReplayController::Reset (SSR_ReplayController.mqh 1268-1293) calls only PublishRewind(cut) at 1286 and never re-publishes OnSessionStart (the only place m_balance is reset, line 579), so after Reset the log is empty and the whole session's realised P/L, fees and swap remain in m_balance. Everything derived (Equity 971, FloatingPL, LotForRisk via Equity at 767/797, prop evaluation, statistics) reads that figure, and RestoreFrom 1221/1253 recomputes balance from the log so the 'balance replayed from the trades' warning does fire. T9_Trading.mq5 330-363 asserts only ByTicket/OpenCount and never the balance, so the leak is untested.

Provable from source and reachable through a first-class button. In OnRewind the 'continue' at 642-643 drops a position placed after the cut before UnwindLegsAfter (646) and before the un-fill refund branch (660-690), so none of the money it moved is reversed: the entry commission (754, or 356 on a pending fill), every leg's realised - fee (222) and any accrued swap (427). The position is not copied to m_pos[keep], so the AccrueSwap restatement at 701 cannot refund its swap either, and no other code recomputes m_balance from the surviving log (only RestoreFrom 1167-1221 does, on file load). The Reset path is confirmed end to end: Panel 2241/2248 -> GroupPort.Reset 425-436 -> CSSRReplayController::Reset, which calls PublishRewind(cut) at 1286 with cut = timeline start and never re-runs OnSessionStart, the only code that restores m_balance = m_balance_initial (579). The host configures the account once, before Load (SSReplayStandalone 1167-1169), so a Reset leaves an empty trade log with the whole session's realised P/L, commissions and swap still in m_balance - and Equity(), LotForRisk sizing off Equity, the prop evaluation and the save-file balance check all read that figure. The test the finder names (T10.9, 'an order placed after the cut simply never existed', SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5 675-689) asserts only Total() == 0 on an open position with commission 0 from e.Init(), so the leak is invisible to the suite.

Provable and reachable through the product's headline feature. OnRewind (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:640-643) `continue`s past any position whose placed msc > cut, so it is dropped from m_pos without any of its money being reversed: the entry commission subtracted at line 754 / 356, every leg's realised-fee added at line 222, and the swap moved at line 427 all stay in m_balance. The only reversal code (UnwindLegsAfter 263-291 and the un-fill branch 660-690) sits after the continue. Grep of m_balance writers (222, 273, 356, 427, 563, 579, 664, 754, 1167, 1221) shows nothing recomputes the balance from the log after a rewind, and OnSessionStart - the only place m_balance is reset to m_balance_initial - is published exactly once, from Load (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:837), never from Reset or a step-back. Every backward path lands here: SeekTo/step-back (controller 1240), Reset (controller 1286, which cuts to timeline.start_msc and therefore drops the ENTIRE session's trades while keeping their P/L, commission and swap in the balance), and checkpoint restore (1644). Verified from the leg struct and OnRewind. OnRewind (634-702) resets trail_peak/mae/mfe/risk_at_entry only inside the pending-un-fill branch (676-679); a position placed before the cut and still open is copied forward untouched (692-694), keeping the sl a future ApplyTrailing wrote. ApplyTrailing (302-323) only ever raises a long's sl (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`), so the future stop is never retracted, and on the first re-emitted tick CheckStops 526-527 compares the current bid to it and 539/543 books a SL close at StopFill (492-511) = bid - slip. GroupPort MarketAt/Market apply SetTrailing to every new trade when m_trail_points > 0 (SSR_GroupPort.mqh 1061-1063), so the trigger is one panel setting, not an exotic path. Modify (844-853) and BreakEven (920-927) write sl/tp with no versioning either, so a stop moved in the deleted future also survives.

Provable from source. SSRTradeLeg (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh 144-168) records volume/price/msc/realised/fee/closing/prev_swap_locked/prev_swap_from_msc/prev_ambiguous and nothing about sl, tp, trail_peak, mae or mfe, so there is no snapshot for a rewind to restore. OnRewind (634-702) writes sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe only inside the pending-un-fill branch (670-679); a position that was already open at the cut keeps every value the deleted future set. ApplyTrailing (302-323) ratchets one way only ('if(want > m_pos[i].sl)' for a long), so a stop trailed up in the deleted future is never lowered again, and CheckStops 526-527 compares the re-emitted bid against it, closing at StopFill (492-511) with reason SL. GroupPort 1060-1064 does arm trailing automatically on every risk-sized trade when m_trail_points > 0, so the precondition is a user setting, not an exotic path. Severity trimmed from HIGH: the fabricated SL close needs trailing armed or a Modify/BreakEven in the deleted future; what is unconditional for every rewound open position is stale mae/mfe (and spread_at_exit on a re-opened leg), which corrupts reported excursions rather than the balance.

Confirmed from source and reachable without any unusual user action. SSRTradeLeg carries no sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe, and OnRewind (634-702) rewrites those fields only inside the pending-un-fill branch (676-679); a position that was already open before the cut keeps whatever sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe the deleted future gave it. ApplyTrailing (302-323) only ever ratchets the long stop up (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`) / the short stop down, so a stop trailed in the deleted future can never be walked back, and CheckStops (526-527) compares the re-emitted bid to that stale level. The trailing path is armed automatically, not manually: GroupPort.MarketAt applies m_trail_points to every new trade (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:1062-1063) and GroupPort.SetTrailing back-applies it to everything already open (811-829), so one typed trailing distance in the panel puts every subsequent trade on this path. The same hole covers a manual Modify (844-853) or BreakEven (920-927) performed in the deleted future. What the user observes: they step back to a moment when the trade was in profit, the very next re-emitted tick books it as 'stop loss hit' (auto-pause announces it) at a level the replay has just un-happened, and the loss lands in m_balance. That is future price data leaking across a rewind into a real money outcome, which is exactly the guarantee the file's own REWIND CORRECTNESS header claims, so HIGH is right.

The mechanism is provable: BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) compares p.sl/p.tp against the whole cached m_bar low/high and never against open_msc or the running mae (293-300); m_bar is the full minute up to the pump-window end (OnBarContext 593-598; ClipBar keeps 'everything in this minute UP TO the window's end - including the part an earlier pump already emitted', SSR_ReplayController.mqh 446-459). CheckStops 537-541 therefore books ClosePosition(StopFill, SSR_CLOSE_SL, true) - a loss plus slippage - even when every tick after the entry stayed above the stop, and the fill-time flag at 371-384 has the same whole-bar test. BUT the claim's own numbers are self-refuting: with 'SL 5 points below that bar's low' the test `m_bar.low <= p.sl` is FALSE and no ambiguity is raised. The defect needs the stop ABOVE the bar's earlier low, which the title states correctly.

The finding's core premise is that the engine's own synthesised tick order is evidence about what happened. The file states the opposite at lines 11-20 ('that ORDER IS OUR ASSUMPTION, not the market's behaviour'), and it is true: an M1 bar cannot say whether the minute's low printed before or after the instant the user clicked Buy mid-minute, so for a mid-minute entry whose stop sits under that minute's low the outcome genuinely is unknowable and the pessimistic-plus-flag policy (R11) is exactly what is documented. The one case where unhappened price would be used is already guarded twice: ClipBar (ReplayController 240-279) rebuilds a forming bar from only the ticks up to the pump window end, and BarIsAmbiguousFor 156-158 rejects a cached bar the current tick does not live in. 'Every synthesised tick after the entry was above the stop' is precisely the self-flattery the design refuses, and the trade is flagged rather than silently booked, with AmbiguousPercent reporting the fraction. No defect provable from source; at most a possible refinement (weighting by entry time within the minute), which would itself require inventing intra-minute order.

reasons: Both halves of the claim fail. (1) Semantics: SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is defined by MT5 as the amount in the margin currency required to open ONE LOT - it is not contract size, and when a symbol publishes it the terminal uses it instead of the contract-size/leverage formula. Assigning it straight to m_margin_per_lot (588-590) and multiplying by volume in UsedMargin (935-944) is therefore the documented arithmetic, not a missing leverage division; the premise 'several brokers publish the contract size there' is asserted, not shown, and is contradicted by the property's definition. (2) 'Silently overrides InpMarginLot' is wrong: the input is declared as a fallback - SSReplayStandalone.mq5:94 `input double InpMarginLot = 0.0; // Margin per lot (fallback; 0 = not modelled)` - and SetMarginPerLot(InpMarginLot) runs at setup (1168) precisely so that the symbol value, when present, wins at OnSessionStart, with the code comment at 585-587 saying so. Note also that the value is never guaranteed to exist on the replay symbol: CloneMoneyProperties (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh 271-291) does NOT clone SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL, and spike A1 (SSR_A1_SymbolLifecycle.mq5:96) exists to measure whether CustomSymbolCreate carries it over. What genuinely remains is only a refinement: SYMBOL_MARGIN_*_RATE multipliers and margin-currency conversion are not applied.

The MQL5 premise is wrong. SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is defined as the amount in margin currency required to open ONE LOT, and where it is non-zero the terminal computes margin = lots * MARGIN_INITIAL * margin rate - ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE does not divide it. So 'v * m_margin_per_lot' (935-944) is the documented arithmetic, not a 100-500x error; the 'brokers publish contract size there' scenario is broker-misreporting speculation the finder itself cannot verify. Two supporting premises also fail: the value is read for the symbol passed to OnSessionStart, which is the ORIGIN broker symbol (host calls g_ctrl.Load(origin, ...), controller 837), so nothing about CustomSymbolCreate property inheritance is involved; and the 'silent override' of InpMarginLot is the documented intent - the host input is labelled 'Margin per lot (fallback; 0 = not modelled)' (SSReplayStandalone.mq5 line 94), a fallback by definition yielding to the instrument's own figure. Left at LOW severity only for the cosmetic point that the override is not logged.

Two of the three legs of this finding are wrong. (1) 'No leverage division' misreads MT5: SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is documented as the amount in margin currency required to open ONE LOT - it is already the per-lot margin, so using it directly in UsedMargin() (935-944) is the correct arithmetic, not a missing division. It is 0 for Forex-calculation symbols (margin not modelled, exactly what the comment at 585-587 says) and non-zero for futures/CFD-style symbols where it genuinely is the per-lot initial margin. The premise that 'several brokers publish the contract size there' is speculation that contradicts the field's documented meaning and cannot be settled from this repo. (2) 'Silently overrides the user's explicit InpMarginLot' is the documented design: the input is labelled 'Margin per lot (fallback; 0 = not modelled)' (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:94), and SetMarginPerLot(InpMarginLot) at 1168 runs before Load at 1252 precisely so the instrument's own figure wins when it declares one. A fallback being overridden by the real value is the stated contract. The stopout scenario additionally needs InpStopout > 0, which defaults to 0. At most an improvement: the panel/log could name which source the margin figure came from.
trading-exec-7.corrected: Not a defect as described. SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is per-lot margin in the margin currency by MT5 definition, so using it directly needs no leverage division, and InpMarginLot is documented as a fallback the symbol value is meant to override (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:94, engine comment 585-587). The only residual gap is that the SYMBOL_MARGIN_*_RATE multipliers and margin-currency conversion are ignored, and that the replay symbol may not carry the property at all since CloneMoneyProperties does not copy it.

reasons: Traced end to end with no guard anywhere. BreakEven (920-927) sets sl = open_price after only a state check; for a long open_price = FillPrice(true,true) = ask + slip (743), which is above the bid by the whole spread plus slippage. On the next tick CheckStops 526-527 evaluates `px <= sl` with px = m_bid and fires; with tp == 0 BarIsAmbiguousFor returns false at 160-161, so 543 closes at StopFill = min(sl, bid) - slip = bid - slip, i.e. a guaranteed loss of spread + 2x slippage booked as SSR_CLOSE_SL. Modify (844-853) writes any sl/tp with no side check. No caller filters: GroupPort BreakEven (867-874) and BreakEvenAll (899-914) only null-check m_acct, and the panel wires them raw ('be' button SSR_Panel.mqh:2116, per-row action 2679) with no price comparison.

Provable from source and stronger than the finding states. Since bid <= ask always, the new stop is at or above the comparison price from the moment it is written, so the very next tick satisfies px <= sl and ClosePosition books reason SL at StopFill = min(sl, bid) - slip (492-511) - a loss of the spread plus slippage, counted as a losing trade and announced by the SSR_PAUSE_ON_SL watcher. No guard exists upstream either: GroupPort.BreakEven 867-874 and BreakEvenAll 899-914 pass the ticket through untouched, and Modify 844-853 writes any sl/tp with no comparison to m_bid/m_ask. A terminal rejects a long SL above bid (invalid stops) and leaves the position running, so nothing about this depends on unsettled runtime behaviour.

Confirmed and easy to reach. BreakEven (920-927) writes sl = open_price with only a state check, and open_price for a long is FillPrice(true,true) = ask + slip, i.e. strictly above the current bid; Modify (844-853) writes any sl/tp with no side check; GroupPort.BreakEven / BreakEvenAll (867-915) add none either. CheckStops (526-527) then reads px = bid <= sl as a stop hit and StopFill (492-511) takes min(level, price) - slip, so the position is closed at bid - slip: a certain loss of spread + slippage, booked with reason SL, counted as a losing trade by Statistics, and announced by auto-pause. The worst reachable case is the panel's one-press BreakEvenAll, which moves EVERY open stop to its entry including positions currently in drawdown - each of those has open_price on the wrong side of the market and is force-closed at market on the next tick, so a user who meant 'protect my winners' silently liquidates their losers. A real terminal rejects the modification ('invalid stops') and the position keeps running. MEDIUM is right: reachable through ordinary UI use and it manufactures closed losing trades, but each individual loss is small (spread + 2x slippage) and nothing beyond the virtual account is touched.
trading-exec-8.corrected: BreakEven sets a long's stop to its ask-side fill price and CheckStops tests it against the bid, so the condition px <= sl is already satisfied when the stop is written: pressing 'be' before price has advanced past the entry spread closes the trade on the very next tick as an SL. This holds even with zero spread and zero slippage, where sl == open_price == bid triggers on equality (a flat 'stop loss' in the statistics). Modify() has the same missing wrong-side check, and neither path marks the close as a rejected modification.

reasons: FillPrice (120-126) adds m_exec.slippage_points unconditionally on the opening side, and CheckPendings 345 uses it for all four pending types including BUY_LIMIT/SELL_LIMIT whose triggers are `m_ask <= request_price` / `m_bid >= request_price` (335-336). When the trigger tick is at or near the limit the fill exceeds the limit by up to the slippage distance, while the file's own reasoning at 486-490 fills TP exactly at its level (544) because a limit fills at its price or better - so the two limit cases really are modelled inconsistently. Effective only with InpSlippage > 0 (default 0.0, SSReplayStandalone.mq5:91), and a gapped trigger can still fill better than the limit, hence LOW. One sub-claim is wrong: risk_at_entry is recomputed at fill from the actual open_price (350-353), so it does not understate the risk; only the lot size from OpenPendingWithRisk/LotForRisk (797) is computed off the requested price.

The code path is as described: FillPrice (120-126) adds slippage_points unconditionally and its own comment calls it 'the price a market order actually gets'; CheckPendings 345 uses it for all four pending types, so a BUY_LIMIT triggered at m_ask <= request_price is filled at m_ask + slip, which can land above the limit. That contradicts the file's own reasoning at 486-490, where a take profit is treated as a limit that fills at its level precisely because a limit does not suffer adverse slippage - and it is a divergence from terminal semantics, where deviation applies to market orders, not to limit entries. Kept only as an improvement: exec.slippage_points comes from InpSlippage, default 0.0 (host line 91), so the path is inert unless the user opts in.

Confirmed from source: FillPrice (120-126) adds slippage unconditionally and CheckPendings (345) uses it for all four pending types, so a BUY_LIMIT triggered at m_ask == request_price fills at request_price + slip - worse than its own limit. For BUY_STOP/SELL_STOP that is correct (a stop is a market order, as StopFill's comment argues), but the same file argues at 486-490 that a limit fills at its price or better and honours that for take-profit (544), so the treatment of entry limits is internally inconsistent, and risk_at_entry computed off the slipped fill no longer matches the risk the user sized at the request price. Impact is genuinely small: InpSlippage defaults to 0 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:91), so nothing happens unless the user opts into slippage, and then the error is bounded by the configured points on limit entries only. LOW stands - no upgrade, since the direction is pessimistic (it never flatters a result) and it cannot leak future data or corrupt the balance beyond that bounded amount.
trading-exec-9.corrected: FillPrice (120-126) applies adverse slippage to pending-order fills of every type, so BUY_LIMIT/SELL_LIMIT entries (CheckPendings 335-336, 345) can fill worse than their limit price - inconsistent with the TP treatment the file argues for at 486-490 and implements at 544. Only with InpSlippage > 0 (default 0). risk_at_entry is NOT affected: it is recomputed from the real open_price at 350-353; the residual inaccuracy is only the lot size, sized off the request price in OpenPendingWithRisk 797.

reasons: Numerator and denominator genuinely count different populations. m_ambiguous_count is incremented both for still-OPEN positions at fill time (CheckPendings 381-382) and for closes (BookExit 236-240), while AmbiguousPercent (999-1003) divides by ClosedCount(), which counts only state == SSR_POS_CLOSED (988-994). One ambiguous open fill with one unambiguous closed trade prints 100%, two print 200%, and with ambiguous fills but zero closes it prints 0%. The figure is not internal: it is published to external clients as SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS (SSR_Publisher.mqh:206) and rendered by ToString (1266-1274).

Mismatched numerator and denominator, provable from source. m_ambiguous_count is incremented for a still-OPEN position at the pending-fill site (371-383) as well as for closes in BookExit (236-240), and RestoreFrom 1216-1217 counts the flag on positions in any state, while AmbiguousPercent (999-1003) divides by ClosedCount(), which counts only state == SSR_POS_CLOSED (988-994). So one ambiguous open fill against one clean closed trade reports 100%, two report 200%, and the figure is user-visible: ToString 1266-1273 prints it and Publisher 206 exports it to SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS. The converse also holds - ambiguous open fills with nothing closed yet report 0.0%. LOW, since it misstates an honesty metric rather than the account.

The arithmetic mismatch is real: m_ambiguous_count is incremented for OPEN positions at fill (381-383) as well as for closes (236-240), while AmbiguousPercent's denominator is ClosedCount() (988-994), which counts only state == CLOSED - so the ratio can exceed 100%, and conversely reports a flat 0.0 while ambiguous fills are open but nothing has closed yet. But the blast radius is far smaller than the finding implies: the user-facing honesty figure in the statement, the CSV and the HTML report does NOT come from this method. SSR_Statistics.mqh computes ambiguous_trades over closed positions only (loop filter at 407-408 `!p.IsClosed() -> continue`, count at 463-464) and divides by out.trades (544), which is correct. CSSRTradingEngine::AmbiguousPercent has exactly two consumers: ToString() (1271, a log line) and the Publisher's SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS global export (SSR_Publisher.mqh:206). So nothing a trader reads in the statement is wrong; a debug log line and one integration global can read >100%. Downgraded from LOW to IMPROVEMENT accordingly.
trading-exec-11.corrected: Real numerator/denominator mismatch, but it affects only CSSRTradingEngine::ToString()'s log line and the SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS global export (SSR_Publisher.mqh:206). The statement, CSV and HTML honesty figure is computed independently in SSR_Statistics.mqh over closed trades only and is correct, so no user-facing report shows the inflated percentage.

Provable: Open() 705-756 validates capacity, volume > 0, a price for pendings and nothing else; the risk engine already holds m_vol_min/m_vol_max/m_vol_step and a rounding helper (SSR_RiskEngine.mqh 23-31, 49-56, 73-74) that only the LotForRisk paths use. trading-exec-12.corrected: Accurate as a validation gap, but reachable only via the Publisher external path (gated by InpAllowTrade, default false) and hand-written strategies; all panel paths are already rounded by LotForRisk, and the account arithmetic stays self-consistent at any positive volume, so the effect is presentational fidelity rather than incorrect money.

reasons: AccrueSwap (401-430) counts day boundaries by integer division of the tick's msc (407, 418) with no day-of-week and no rollover-hour test; a repo-wide grep finds no triple-swap or Wednesday logic. So a position held 23:00 to 01:00 is charged one day and one held 00:30 to 23:30 nothing, exactly as claimed, and a Wednesday-to-Thursday hold is charged 1x rather than 3x. This is an acknowledged simplification (comment 388-399, 'per REPLAY day held') rather than a latent fault, which matches the IMPROVEMENT severity. One inaccuracy: the boundary is midnight of the replay tick clock, i.e. broker/server time carried in MqlTick.time_msc, not UTC.

No defect, and the semantics are partly misread. m_now_msc carries tick server time, so 'm_now_msc / SSR_MSC_PER_DAY' (86400000, SSR_Types.mqh 33) buckets on SERVER-time midnight, not UTC midnight as the title says; the division is over positive epoch milliseconds, so no truncation hazard. The second example in the claim - opened 00:30, closed 23:30, charged nothing - is correct behaviour for a rollover model, not a defect. What remains is the absence of a triple-swap day and a configurable rollover hour, which the header at 388-400 states as the model ('per REPLAY day held') and which the finder concedes is consistent with it; note also that counting calendar-day boundaries already charges the weekend days a Friday-to-Monday hold crosses. A missing broker-convention refinement in an explicitly documented model is not a bug.

The description of the code is accurate - AccrueSwap (401-430) divides m_now_msc by SSR_MSC_PER_DAY and there is no day-of-week or rollover-hour logic anywhere - but this is the documented model, not a defect. The method's own header states the rule it implements ('Swap, per REPLAY day held... on the replay calendar, not the real one'), the restatement design is what makes it rewind-safe, and InpSwapLong/InpSwapShort default to 0 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:92-93) so no user sees any swap unless they opt in and choose the numbers themselves. The claim's second example refutes itself: a position opened 00:30 and closed 23:30 crossing no midnight should be charged nothing, which is what happens. What remains is the triple-swap Wednesday and the missing rollover hour - a modelling simplification that under-states cost by a bounded, user-configured amount on one weekday. The finder already rated it IMPROVEMENT; it is not a bug, just an unimplemented refinement.
trading-exec-14.corrected: AccrueSwap (401-430) charges swap per crossed midnight of the REPLAY/server tick clock (not UTC), with no rollover hour and no triple-swap day: a 23:00-01:00 hold pays 1x, a 00:30-23:30 hold pays nothing, and a Wednesday-to-Thursday hold pays 1x instead of 3x. Documented simplification (comment 388-399), so a modelling gap rather than a fault.

reasons: Traced both loops. The opening sweep (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:352-364) walks ChartFirst/ChartNext with no `id == ChartID()` exclusion and closes every chart whose symbol ends in SSR_SYMBOL_SUFFIX+InpSlot, so a script dropped on a chart of e.g. EURUSD.SSR9 with InpSlot=9 closes its own chart three Log lines in. Cleanup() (5466-5474) has the same shape. Two things I cannot settle from source: (a) that MT5 terminates a script when its host chart closes (real MT5 semantics, but runtime), and (b) that a user drops this on a replay chart rather than a broker chart, which is the only way the tail can match _Symbol. The Cleanup half of the claim is additionally unreachable on its own.

Source confirms both loops lack any ChartID() exclusion: the opening sweep (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:352-364, tail = SSR_SYMBOL_SUFFIX + InpSlot built at 350) and Cleanup (5468-5475, `if(ChartSymbol(id) == rsym) ChartClose(id);`) close by symbol only. But everything that makes it a defect is runtime/user-dependent and cannot be settled from source: (a) whether MetaTrader terminates a script when the chart it runs on is closed by that same script, (b) that the user drops the script on a chart of a slot-InpSlot replay symbol. The Cleanup path is narrower than claimed: rsym = SSRReplaySymbolName(origin, slot), and with InpSymbol empty origin == _Symbol, so the host chart's symbol can only equal rsym if the user explicitly typed InpSymbol as the broker symbol while standing on its replay chart. The stated side effects are also softer than claimed - Log() does FileFlush per line (222) so the file holds everything up to the sweep, and MQL5 closes open handles when a program unloads, so 'g_fh unclosed' costs nothing.

The missing guard is real: neither the opening sweep (l.352-363) nor Cleanup() (l.5468-5476) compares id against ChartID(). Whether MetaTrader then kills the running script is runtime behaviour I cannot settle from this tree, so POTENTIAL_RISK, not CONFIRMED. Severity is over-stated at MEDIUM on two grounds. First, reachability: the sweep only reaches the script's own chart if the user drops a QA script onto a chart of the replay symbol for the slot this run uses - a corner of a diagnostic tool, not normal product use, and nothing about the product, the money arithmetic or the virtual-trading guarantee is touched. Second, the Cleanup() half of the claim is close to unreachable: it fires only when _Symbol == rsym exactly, and in that configuration (origin typed as InpSymbol, script on the <origin>.SSRN chart) the opening sweep at l.359 has already closed that same chart 5100 lines earlier, so the run never reaches Cleanup. The live path is the sweep alone.
qa-smoke-6.corrected: The self-close is reachable only through the opening sweep (352-364), and only when the script's own chart carries a symbol ending in `.SSR<InpSlot>` - i.e. it is dropped on a replay chart. Cleanup() at 5466 cannot self-close independently: rsym = SSRReplaySymbolName(origin, slot) always ends in that same tail (SSR_SymbolNaming.mqh:36-47), so any chart Cleanup would match was already matched - and closed - by the opening sweep, which would have killed the run long before Cleanup is reached. One `if(id == ChartID()) { id = nxt; continue; }` in the sweep is the whole fix.

reasons: Both branches the claim rests on are arithmetically impossible. ViewOffset = first-(visible-1) with a `off<0 -> 0` clamp (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:124-125). At the right edge under CHART_SHIFT, whichever way MetaTrader defines CHART_VISIBLE_BARS, first_visible_bar can never EXCEED visible-1: if `visible` is window capacity in bar slots and the shift gap eats G slots, first = visible-G-1 so off = -G -> clamped to 0; if `visible` counts only slots holding bars, first = visible-1 so off = 0 exactly. There is no 'systematically positive' branch, so the 'permanent false detach on every chart' outcome cannot occur. The 'clamped to 0' branch is also not the described defect: Redraw's snap is gated on `ViewOffset(...) > 0` (line 575), the SAME clamped number, so inside the dead zone the snap does not fire either - the tool does not 'keep yanking the user back'. The shift merely inflates both the detach threshold and the snap threshold by the same G bars, and because one formula feeds both they stay consistent by construction (the finding cites that shared use as an aggravator; it is the mitigation). What is genuinely wrong is only the doc comment at lines 111-113, whose premise ignores the CHART_SHIFT set at line 315.

The contradiction is real in source: ApplyPolicy sets CHART_SHIFT=true (line 315) on every opened AND discovered chart, while ViewOffset (118-126) assumes bar 0 sits at the right border. Which branch occurs is genuinely unsettleable here. But the two branches are not equally likely: CHART_VISIBLE_BARS is a window-capacity figure, so with the shift gap the right-edge CHART_FIRST_VISIBLE_BAR is SMALLER than visible-1, making 'off' negative and clamped to 0. That is the benign branch, and it is also why no false detach storm has been reported. Its impact is a dead zone equal to the shift width: a scroll of fewer than ~(shift bars + 3) registers as offset 0, so DetectScroll never detaches and the terminal's own autoscroll keeps yanking the user forward - the exact UX the feature exists to kill, but only for small scrolls; larger ones work. The catastrophic branch (permanent detach on first bar) would fail 100% of sessions and is the less likely reading. Severity stays MEDIUM: UX-only, no money arithmetic, no leak, and recoverable with F or any pause-play.

But the finding's two claimed outcomes do not follow. (a) The "systematically positive -> permanent false detach" branch is arithmetically impossible: under the alternative reading (visible counts only slots holding bars) off is 0 or 1 at the right edge, and DetectScroll requires off > SSR_SCROLL_DETACH_BARS (3), so no detach. (b) "Redraw keeps yanking the user back" is wrong: Redraw's snap at line 574-575 is gated on ViewOffset(...) > 0, so inside the dead zone it does not fire at all. The mechanism is provable. chart-14.corrected: The double count holds regardless of how synchronously ChartOpen publishes the chart to ChartFirst/ChartSymbol: if the new chart is visible to its own Sync, m_count = 1+opened; if it lags by one pass, m_count = opened - either way m_count grows in step with `opened`, so the effective ceiling is ~SSR_MAX_CHARTS/2 (8 opens) rather than 16. chart-1.corrected: SSR_SPEED_MAX is not open-ended at the clock: CSSRReplayClock::Advance multiplies wall delta by speed_x100/100 with no special case (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:94-111), so MAX is literally 1000x. reasons: Traced end to end and confirmed. Scan() increments other_live_charts for any chart that is neither the replay nor the origin symbol and is not a replay symbol (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:59-60), but SSRLeakReport::IsClean() tests only origin_in_watch and origin_charts (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108), Advice() returns "" whenever IsClean() (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:91-92), SSRLeakReport::ToString() short-circuits to the literal 'no leak' on the same test (line 115-116), and SSR_GroupPort.mqh:167-169 copies only LeaksClean()/LeakAdvice() into the port, which SSR_Panel.mqh:1892-1894 renders as T(SSR_S_CHARTS_CLEAN) = 'clean'. grep confirms other_live_charts has no reader outside the increment, the struct and the log-only ToString at line 104, and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART is never assigned anywhere. Severity LOW rather than higher: a correlated instrument is a judgement call the guard cannot make (it has no correlation input), so the defensible fix is surfacing the count, not folding it into IsClean.

The observations are accurate - other_live_charts is incremented at line 60, appears only in ToString (which the Expert never prints) and the struct, and IsClean (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108) tests origin only - but the scope is deliberate and correct. IsClean is documented as the origin-symbol contract, and the leak guard's whole subject is the instrument being replayed: it can act on that one (HideOrigin) and can act on nothing else, as the file header says up front. Counting every non-replay chart as dirty would mark essentially every real terminal permanently dirty - any watchlist chart, any unrelated pair - which turns the only leak indicator into noise the user learns to ignore, a strictly worse outcome for the blindness guarantee than the present origin-focused signal. Nor is this future data of the replayed series: a live correlated chart the user opened themselves shows today's price of a different instrument, and the panel's 'clean' is a statement about the origin, not a claim that the desk contains no live prices.

The factual half is verified - other_live_charts is incremented at line 60 and read only by ToString() (line 104), and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART is never assigned - but the defect framing does not hold. IsClean() (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108) deliberately scopes a leak to the ORIGIN symbol, and that is the only scope the code can justify: Scan() counts every chart whose symbol is neither the replay symbol nor the origin nor a replay symbol (SSRIsReplaySymbol), which includes any unrelated instrument a trader happens to have open for other work. Nothing in this class measures correlation, so the finding's "highly correlated instrument" is an inference the code has no basis for; folding other_live_charts into IsClean() would make the panel declare a leak on essentially every real desktop and would drown the origin-symbol warning it exists to deliver. The residue is an unused struct field plus unused enum vocabulary, i.e. an improvement, not a bug.
chart-9.corrected: other_live_charts is write-only and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART is never assigned, but excluding it from IsClean is a deliberate, defensible scope choice: surfacing every unrelated open chart would leave the indicator permanently dirty and therefore ignored. The improvement worth making is logging the count (Leak().ToString() is never printed by the host) or a softer secondary hint, not folding it into IsClean.

MT5 emits CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE only when that property is on and its default is off, so every branch of CSSRSetupPanel::OnChartEvent (:955-996) is dead on a fresh chart. Where I part company with the finder is severity. What the user loses is one convenience - the setup window cannot be dragged - and the fallback is benign: Create() already centres the panel on the tallest step (:531-544), m_placed simply stays false, and the two GlobalVariables are never written, which is not a corruption of anything. No money arithmetic, no future-data leak, no weakening of the virtual-trading guarantee. The secondary point (CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL forced true at :970 instead of restored) sits inside the same dead code and has no effect at all. A documented-but-absent feature plus a small amount of dead code -> LOW, not MEDIUM.

The numbers are not hidden (step-3 recap :886-890 and the host's prop.ToString() log), and 0 meaning "no limit" matches the max_days convention, so the defect is the missing keyboard-side validation, not a silent deletion.

(5) CSSRPropEvaluation is not driven at all during a jump (OnClock is published only at l.1029/1104) and is voided, not failed, by NotifyRestored. The comment at SSR_SessionManager.mqh:324-333 is indeed stale for the dialog path (TradingEngine::RestoreFrom zeroes m_count at l.1165, after the wind-forward loop), but every downstream effect named is neutralised, and the tick volume is far smaller than claimed. The exposure is on a routine path, not an exotic one: the host saves the whole session on every OnDeinit reason including REASON_CHARTCHANGE (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2133-2142), and the dialog's Replace branch overwrites in place (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:242) right after telling the user there is no undo.

reasons: The asymptotic shape is provable: GetNth rescans all m_ent_count entries per call (l.335-342) with no per-section or per-key index, and its three callers fetch by index inside a loop - TradingEngine::RestoreFrom for `pos` (l.1172-1177) and `leg` (l.1225-1231) and CSSRStatsEngine::RestoreFrom for `e` (SSR_Statistics.mqh:645-651). Whether that is perceptible is a wall-time question about MQL5 string comparison that cannot be settled from source, and the finder concedes it is unmeasured, so this cannot exceed POTENTIAL_RISK. Count() is called once per key, not per row, so it contributes O(entries), not a second quadratic term.

The algorithmic shape is exactly as described: GetNth walks all m_ent_count entries per call (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:331-344) and so does Count (l.322-329), and three callers index rows in a loop - TradingEngine::RestoreFrom for `pos` (l.1172-1176) and `leg` (l.1225-1230) and CSSRStatsEngine::RestoreFrom for `e` (SSR_Statistics.mqh:645-652). Nothing indexes by section or key. The cost is therefore quadratic in file size, and Restore runs on the host's OnInit path (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1483) with the terminal blocked. I cannot confirm the wall-time claim from source, and the stated operation count is inflated.

The O(rows x entries) shape is real - GetNth rescans from index 0 each call (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:331-344) and all three callers fetch by index in a loop (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1172-1176, 1225-1230; SSR_Statistics.mqh:645-650) - but the magnitude and the cost model are both overstated, which is what settles the impact. GetNth returns early at the match, so the i-th row costs its own index, not m_ent_count; and the loop body short-circuits on `m_ent_sec[i] != m_cursor` first, so the overwhelming majority of iterations are one int compare, not a string compare. Working from the section order Save emits (session, settings, streams, account, execution, positions, equity), the absolute worst case is ~1.2M iterations for pos, ~10M for leg and ~28M for e - about 39M cheap int compares, not 110M key comparisons. That worst case also needs 512 trades AND a full 4096-sample equity ring; a realistic training session (tens of trades) lands around 50ms. Wall time is unmeasurable from source, so POTENTIAL_RISK, but under the impact lens the user observes nothing in normal use and at most a sub-second hitch at the ceiling.

The realistic shape for a long replay with few trades is a full 4,096-sample equity ring against ~4,600 entries, i.e. roughly 19 million - and a typical short training session with a few hundred samples is a few hundred thousand. Real O(n^2) worth fixing with a key index, but not evidently a user-visible stall.

reasons: Traced the whole path. CSSRPanel::Text() (SSR_Panel.mqh:190-207) takes its fast path ONLY when m_cache[slot]==text && m_cache_x/y match && m_w.Exists(id), and on that path it *writes* OBJPROP_COLOR every time - so the object's colour is refreshed on every hit, never left to drift while the fast path is being taken. The stale-colour outcome needs the opposite combination: a panel-level MISS whose (text,x,y) still equal the widget cache's recorded triple. A panel miss can only come from (a) a different text, (b) a different x/y - both of which are inside the widget fingerprint (SSR_Widgets.mqh:230-233), so Same() returns false anyway - (c) Exists()==false, in which case Same()'s own ObjectFind check (line 88) also returns false, or (d) ClearCache(), which is only ever paired with m_w.RemoveAll()/ForgetAll() (SSR_Panel.mqh:292, 310-312). The one remaining route, slot aliasing (slots 30/31/32 and 12/17 are reused across ids/branches), is closed by HideSheets() (SSR_Panel.mqh:1270, 1284-1340), which m_w.Remove()s - i.e. deletes and Forgets - every sheet object including st1/st2/st3/posmore/poshint/trlbl/setuprow at the top of each repaint, so no cross-branch widget-cache entry survives to be matched. No reachable stale colour; this is a hardening request (a public Invalidate seam), not a defect.

The premise is half true: CSSRPanel::Text() (SSR_Panel.mqh:194-199) does write OBJPROP_COLOR on a hit without telling the widget cache, so m_cn[] can hold a colour the object no longer has. But the stated trigger - "a second panel-level cache miss asks for the recorded colour with the recorded text and position" - is unreachable by construction, not merely by today's clear-them-together accident. A panel miss can only be caused by (a) text differing (then m_ct[k] != text and Same() returns false), (b) x or y differing (then fp differs, because Label folds x and y into the fingerprint at SSR_Widgets.mqh:232-233), (c) !m_w.Exists(id) (then Same()'s own ObjectFind at SSR_Widgets.mqh:88 returns false), or (d) slot out of [0,SSR_SLOTS) - and in case (d) the fast path is never taken for that id at all, so no divergence can have been created. Every miss therefore either differs in a fingerprinted field or fails the existence probe. The only remaining path is an independent reset of the panel cache, and ClearCache() is called exactly twice (ctor SSR_Panel.mqh:292, and Create() line 312 one line after m_w.RemoveAll()/ForgetAll()). The one object drawn with m_w.Label() outside Text() ("taglbl", SSR_Panel.mqh:1373) never takes the fast path either. The public Invalidate(id) suggestion is a reasonable hardening, but there is no defect and no latent state to reach without new code.

The divergence is unreachable, and not for the reason given. Two independent structural facts close it. (1) SSR_Panel.mqh:1284-1340 HideSheets() runs at the TOP OF EVERY REPAINT and ObjectDelete()s every sheet-owned id (st1..st7, poshint, trlbl, posmore, ses*, pp_*, pr/pl/pn rows...). Text()'s fast path requires m_w.Exists(id), which is false for all of those at draw time, so the direct OBJPROP_COLOR write never executes for any sheet label. (2) For the ids that DO survive a repaint (title/build/capinfo/clock/prog/spdlbl/spdval/spdmean/stbal/stflt/stopen/stfid/stspread, slots 0-6 and 50-55), the panel cache key (text, x, y) is a strict SUBSET of the widget fingerprint (x, y, col, size, fontlen) + text. A panel-cache MISS therefore implies text, x or y differs from the values recorded by the last Label() call, which in turn guarantees Same() returns false and the full six writes run. I also checked the one path that could break the subset property - two different ids sharing a panel slot (slots 30/31/32 are shared between poshint/posmore/trlbl and st1/st2/st3, slot 50 by five stbal call sites) - and every shared slot belongs exclusively to sheet ids killed by HideSheets, while every persistent id owns a unique slot. No stale semantic colour can be observed. The finder's own stated mechanism (ClearCache and RemoveAll always run together) is not what protects this.

The mechanism is exactly as coded. Slot() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:58-77) stops at the first free-OR-matching slot, Forget() (101-107) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and silently no-ops when the probe lands on a freed earlier slot, and Keep() (91-99) writes a second copy there; nothing but ForgetAll() (Attach/RemoveAll) ever reclaims the orphan. Home-slot collisions are certain at this load: hashing the panel's real names (SSRP_ prefix, ~264 of them in 512 slots) with the file's own FNV-1a gives 53 colliding home slots (e.g. SSRP_lines/SSRP_pn3, SSRP_riskval/SSRP_spdseg0, SSRP_hintrow/SSRP_palette), and the churn that supplies the freed earlier slot is real - HideSheets() Removes ~100 names and 6x SSR_POS_MAX row names at the top of every repaint, and SSR_Panel.mqh:1937-1940 Hides four status names unconditionally per frame. I could not refute the duplicate-slot leak.

The mechanism is fully settled from source. Slot() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:57-76) returns the FIRST free-or-matching slot in an 8-probe run, so once an earlier slot in a probe chain is cleared, a displaced name resolves to it; Forget() (103-108) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and no-ops, and Keep() (86-94) writes a second live copy at the earlier slot, orphaning the later one forever (only ForgetAll(), i.e. Attach-with-changed-chart/prefix or RemoveAll(), reclaims it). Displacement is not hypothetical: I computed FNV-1a exactly as Slot() does over the 107 literal widget ids found in SSR_Panel.mqh under the SSRP_ prefix and 12 of them already land on an occupied home slot - and the real name set is considerably larger (composite widgets add _bg/_fill/_fr/_lb/_lg/_tk/_th/_ac/_lim children, plus 20 spdseg cells, 5 tabs and the list rows). The churn that opens the window is also per-frame and unconditional: Hide() calls Forget() whether or not the object exists (SSR_Widgets.mqh:634-642), and SSR_Panel.mqh:1931-1940 hides stflt/stopen/stspread/stfid on every render while 2085-2099 hides the whole id list, 5 tabs, 20 speed cells and the groove/thumb on every collapse. Two things in the write-up are imprecise rather than wrong, hence the corrected claim.

The logic defect is provable: Slot() (Widgets:70-76) returns the FIRST free-or-matching slot in the 8-probe run, so a hole earlier in a chain shadows a real entry further down; Forget() (Widgets:103-108) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and clears nothing, and the next Keep() writes a second copy at the earlier slot, permanently consuming the shadowed one. Nothing reclaims it (ForgetAll only runs from Attach on a chart/prefix change and from RemoveAll). Reachability is in fact far higher than the finder argues: SSR_Panel.mqh:1284-1340 HideSheets() calls m_w.Remove() on ~80 ids plus 6*SSR_POS_MAX row ids at the top of EVERY repaint, so holes are punched and Forget() is called hundreds of times per second. But the impact is bounded and non-visual: the only certain consequence is attrition of a performance cache - and the objects that churn hardest (all sheet labels) are deleted and recreated every frame anyway, so they never benefited from the cache. The claimed end state (an 8-slot run fully saturated, Slot() returning -1, the 561-write/39.05 ms repaint returning) is a projection, not something the source establishes. No money arithmetic, no future data, no virtual-trading guarantee is touched, so MEDIUM is one step too high.
ui-plumbing-6.corrected: Forget() can resolve to a free earlier slot in the probe chain and clear nothing, after which Keep() stores a duplicate and the off-home entry is orphaned for the life of the cache. Two parts of the finding are wrong, though. (1) The leak is self-limiting, not one slot per Hide at 10 Hz: once the orphan exists it occupies its slot and so removes the free-slot precondition for that chain, and the next Forget/Keep pair re-converges on a stable placement - steady state is a small constant number of orphans per colliding chain, bounded by chain reconfigurations, so the '8-slot probe run fills and the cache switches off' end-state is not established by this code. (2) Contrary to the finding's own evidence, the shadowed duplicate is not always harmless: if another name later occupies the earlier slot, Slot() resolves the name onto the ORPHAN tuple, and Same() then compares the request against a state the object no longer holds - a matching comparison skips the write and leaves the wrong colour/text. That path is neutralised for every Remove()-invalidated name (the object is deleted, so Same()'s ObjectFind check fails) and is only live for Hide()-invalidated names, which are never deleted.

reasons: The arithmetic claim is right - Mix() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:135) is a mod-2^64 polynomial hash, and for the two lowest terms a collision needs no overflow at all: fp = ... + bg*1000003 + edge, so (bg+d, edge-d*1000003) collides for |d|<=16. But the described outcome - two ATTAINABLE states of one widget colliding - does not exist here. I brute-forced every palette: for each of SSR_THEME_RAIL (51 tokens), LIGHT (51) and DARK (35), over all ordered pairs, there is no (bg1,bg2) with |diff|<=16 whose matching (edge1,edge2) differs by exactly -diff*1000003. Zero exact two-term collisions in all three palettes. The only remaining collisions are the overflow ones, which require the full 64-bit difference to vanish - probability ~2^-64 per pair of states, and no call site can be shown to reach one. Label()'s fingerprint is additionally injective in practice (a nonzero colour difference is multiplied by M^2 while the size and font-length terms are bounded by ~16 and ~20, so they cannot cancel it). What survives is a documentation defect: the header's 'NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION' is true of the text half only, and the numeric half is a hash whose collision-freedom is unverified rather than structural. No defect in the shipped build.

The arithmetic is right and the documented invariant at SSR_Widgets.mqh:40-44 ("NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION") is false for the numeric half: Mix() is a * 1000003 + b, so Rect()'s fingerprint is a linear form with bg weighted M=1000003 and edge weighted 1. Since M < 2^24 and (long)color spans 0..0xFFFFFF, (bg+d, edge-d*M) for |d|<=16 collides without any overflow at all, and ButtonC's seven chained Mix calls (SSR_Widgets.mqh:364-365) put bg at M^3 ~ 1e18 where wraparound is genuine. Same() verifies nothing against the object beyond ObjectFind, so a collision would skip all nine writes. What keeps this from being a defect rather than a falsified comment: every colour argument in this codebase is a compile-time palette token (A17 enforces that no colour is written outside SSR_Theme.mqh), the value space is therefore a few dozen constants per role, and the finder states they could exhibit no colliding pair - I could not either. x, y, w and h are small ints whose weights (M^5..M^2) do not overlap their ranges. So the reachable-collision question cannot be settled from source without enumerating every (bg,edge,fg,size) combination actually drawn, and the real, provable content is the broken invariant plus the absence of read-back verification. Severity reduced from MEDIUM: no reachable collision was shown and the palette makes one unlikely.

The arithmetic is right and the state is unreachable, which I settled rather than assumed. The cancellation the finder describes - (bg, edge) vs (bg+d, edge-d*1000003) - is exact, but it needs BOTH members of the pair to exist in the palette and to be two states of the SAME object. I brute-forced it: for all three palettes (RAIL 26, LIGHT 39, DARK 33 distinct colour values behind the 51 tokens) I computed the Rect fingerprint over every bg x edge pair and the ButtonC fingerprint over every bg x edge x fg x size combination (sizes 7-13), all with exact mod-2^64 arithmetic. Zero collisions in every palette. I then ran geometry grids - Rect over x in 0..1599 and y in 0..1199 (1.92M states), Rect over w in 1..599 and h in 1..199, Label over x in 0..799, y in 0..599 for several colours - again zero. So no pair of states this product can ask for collides, and the finder concedes they could not exhibit one either. What survives is a header comment that overclaims ('NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION') for the numeric half - a documentation/verification gap with no reachable user-visible effect, not a MEDIUM defect on a trading panel.
ui-plumbing-7.corrected: Mix() is a mod-2^64 linear/polynomial hash, so the class comment's "NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION" is false for the numeric half of the fingerprint: bg's weight (1000003 in Rect, 1000003^3 in ButtonC) overlaps the 24-bit colour range, so distinct (bg,edge) pairs can share a fingerprint and Same() would skip the write. The defect is the falsified invariant and the missing verification; no colliding pair exists among the 51 compile-time palette tokens actually passed, so no wrong pixel is reachable in the current build.

Traced and it is worse than runtime-contingent - it is deterministic. The last M1 bar exists because a tick landed in it, so for a symbol that has stopped quoting the last quote necessarily satisfies lastbar_open <= last_quote <= lastbar_close, making the test at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:123 true and out.last_msc = lastbar_open-1, discarding a bar that can never receive another tick. The else branch is only taken when the last quote is NEWER than the final bar's close, i.e. when the M1 series is lagging the quote feed. The consumer chain is as claimed: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1075 uses range.last_msc directly as win_end, and CSSRHistoryCatalog exposes the same range. No guard, clamp or later correction exists anywhere on that path.

The arithmetic is exactly as described and checks out against the constants: SSR_MSC_PER_MIN is 60000 (SSR_Types.mqh:31), lastbar_close = lastbar_open + 59999, and the true branch sets out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1, which drops the whole final M1 bar (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:117-125). The forming-bar proxy "last quote falls inside the last bar" is indeed unconditionally true on a closed market, because the tick that created the final bar IS the last quote, and the code tests neither SymbolInfoSessionQuote/SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE nor the lag against wall time. It stays POTENTIAL_RISK under this lens because the conclusion rests entirely on the runtime value SymbolInfoInteger(SYMBOL_TIME_MSC) returns for a closed symbol - plausibly the cached Friday quote (giving the off-by-one), but possibly 0 after a terminal restart or symbol re-select, which takes the else branch and is correct - and that cannot be settled without a terminal. Impact is bounded at one M1 bar on win_end (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1076 uses range.last_msc directly), so LOW is right.

The logic is exactly as described. SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:121-128 uses 'is the symbol's last quote inside the last bar?' as a proxy for 'is that bar still forming', and on a closed market the last quote is ALWAYS inside the last bar (the last bar is by definition the one the last tick built), so the test fires and out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1 drops a bar that can never change again. No session-state check (SymbolInfoSessionQuote, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) or wall-clock-lag check exists to separate the two cases. But the impact under any realistic use is one M1 bar at the far end of a timeline thousands of bars long, and it errs in the SAFE direction: it withholds data, it never exposes anything beyond the horizon, so no future-data or money-arithmetic consequence. The user-visible consequence is that LatestStart/CanStartAt/win_end land one minute earlier than they could - nothing they can perceive, and every downstream consumer stays self-consistent because they all read the same shortened bound. LOW overstates a one-minute conservative bias; this is a boundary-precision cleanup.
data-7.corrected: Correct, and broader than the weekend case: the test fires for ANY last_quote at or before the final bar's close, which includes a stale quote that predates the last bar entirely (a symbol whose M1 was downloaded from the server while it is not being quoted). So the one-minute shortfall applies whenever quoting has stopped or lags the series, not only on a Saturday; the else branch that keeps the full last bar is taken only when the quote feed is ahead of the M1 series.

reasons: The code is as quoted (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:465-472) and the cross-reference holds: SanitizeTicks drops only strictly backwards stamps and deliberately preserves equal ones (SSR_DataValidator.mqh:288-303), so buf[clean-1].time_msc is a stamp other ticks may legitimately share, and cursor=last+1 excludes them on the next page. The whole defect therefore hinges on whether CopyTicksRange can truncate in the middle of a millisecond rather than on a millisecond boundary - undocumented, and not decidable from this source or without a terminal. Plausible and unrefuted, but not provable here. Note one narrowing: the loop's break conditions mean a page only continues when last<hi, so the loss can only occur on a truncated page, never on the final page of a window.

The code is as quoted (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:465-471): `last` is buf[clean-1].time_msc after SanitizeTicks, and cursor = last + 1 so the next CopyTicksRange starts one millisecond later, which drops any remaining ticks carrying `last`. The +1 is genuinely required for the non-truncated case given the half-open lower bound documented at 391-397, and the subsystem does acknowledge equal stamps elsewhere - SanitizeTicks drops only strictly backwards stamps, SSR_DataValidator.mqh:284-288. It stays POTENTIAL_RISK because the loss depends entirely on whether CopyTicksRange can truncate its answer in the middle of a millisecond, which is undocumented, unmeasurable without a terminal and settled nowhere in this source; note also that `clean` is post-sanitisation, so if sanitisation itself trimmed the tail the same boundary applies. The claimed consequence - a missing spike extreme changing whether a virtual stop is hit - is plausible but downstream of an unverifiable premise, so LOW is right.

I cannot refute the arithmetic: at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:460-467 cursor = last + 1 excludes every tick that shares the last accepted stamp, and the file's sibling SanitizeTicks (SSR_DataValidator.mqh:284-288) explicitly preserves equal millisecond stamps, so the subsystem does treat that case as legitimate data. Whether it ever bites depends entirely on undocumented terminal behaviour - whether CopyTicksRange can truncate a range answer part-way through a millisecond - which no amount of source reading settles and the author cannot measure without MT5. Two things keep it at LOW rather than higher. First, the loop only re-pages when a page ends short of hi, and a normal pump asks for ~40 ms of replay time, whose tick count is nowhere near any plausible truncation limit; the truncation path is plausible only in bulk/high-speed windows. Second, the consequence is the loss of a few ticks at a page seam, which can shift a minute's extreme by a tick or two - it does not corrupt account arithmetic or expose future data. Note also that `last` is read from the SANITIZED buffer, so if the sanitizer dropped trailing ticks the resume point is earlier than the raw page end and those re-read ticks are simply re-dropped, which is harmless and still terminates (page guard 64).

Csv() (SSR_Journal.mqh:51-58) replaces only commas, LF and CR; it never doubles a quote nor wraps the field, and no caller sanitises quotes either: CSSRGroupPort::SetTradeTag (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-808) trims and replaces commas only, and the session name arrives straight from the setup panel's editable row (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:804 Row("ses",...,true) / 1175 Str("ses",...)), so arbitrary text including a leading quote is reachable. The tag reaches the CSV at column 3 (Row(), l.75) and the session name at the '# session' header (l.190). What I could NOT confirm is the specific failure shown: a quote in the MIDDLE of a field (the '12" chart' example) is literal for both Excel and pandas - RFC-4180 quoting is only recognised at a field's first character - so that example does not merge rows. Whether a real reader misbehaves therefore depends on the exact value typed, which keeps this at potential.

Source-verifiable: Csv() (SSR_Journal.mqh:51-58) replaces ',' -> ';' and CR/LF -> ' ' but never doubles or wraps a double quote, and it is the only sanitiser applied to m_sess_name, m_sess_seed, SessionKey(), st.Caveat(), p.tag and p.note. SetTradeTag (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-809) strips commas only, and InpSession is a raw MQL5 input string, so a '"' can reach the file. Whether that actually merges rows is a property of the third-party reader (RFC-4180 quoted-field handling in Excel/pandas), not of this source, and the project's own reader (SSR_ClassReport.mqh Split on commas) is unaffected - so this cannot be settled from the code and stays potential. The source half is exactly as described: CloseCharts() walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and closes on a bare symbol match with no `id == ChartID()` exclusion (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:505-522), and it runs from Destroy() (549) which runs from Release() (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:383-391) and from the sink destructor (73-74) and from Create() (318). Path and absence of a guard both verified: CloseCharts matches purely on ChartSymbol(id)==m_symbol with no id==ChartID() exclusion (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:505-522), and in one-window mode the EA IS on the replay chart (g_on_replay_chart, g_replay_chart = ChartID() at EA:1276), where OnDeinit does ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) - documented asynchronous at EA:2186 - and then g_ctrl.Release() -> CSSRCustomSymbolSink::Release (line 383-391, m_own_symbol defaults true) -> Destroy() -> CloseCharts(). It stays POTENTIAL_RISK because whether ChartSymbol reflects a pending ChartSetSymbolPeriod synchronously is terminal behaviour not decidable from source, and because the same race decides whether the symbol delete would have succeeded at all. mt5-symbol-4.corrected: CloseCharts() has no id==ChartID() exclusion, so in one-window teardown (EA:2191-2204) it can ChartClose the EA's own window if the asynchronous switch back to the origin has not landed yet. Skipping ChartID() in the loop (and letting the EA's own chart return to the origin) is the fix.

The finder's own reachability analysis is correct and, having traced it, the state is unreachable, which makes it not a defect under the rubric. CSSRCalendarLines::Draw has exactly one caller, LoadCalendar (Expert:940), which is itself called only from BuildSession (Expert:1282). BuildSession has two call sites - OnInit (2080) and the pick-the-start handler (2555) - and they are mutually exclusive per program instance: when picking, OnInit returns INIT_SUCCEEDED at 2073 before reaching 2080, and the handler branch is gated on g_picking, which it clears at 2530. g_cal.Load() therefore runs at most once per instance, so no index in the collection is ever reused for a different event while its object exists. Index-based naming is a fragile convention worth replacing with an event-derived key, but there is no current path that pins a stale event, and the finding says so itself.

The state is unreachable in this product, as the finding itself concedes, and I confirmed the enclosing control flow rather than taking that on trust. reasons: Group() does return an un-refused, half-built shift-0 group, but only on a narrower precondition than the finder describes, and more fields are wrong than claimed. Trace: crossing into an older group hits the early `if(seen == shift && open_set) return true;` at 104-105, so a complete group is returned there. Line 136 is reached only when the backward walk never leaves group 0 - i.e. EVERY bar in the buffer belongs to the requested shift-0 group. In that case out.open was last overwritten at 125 from m_m1[0] (the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold), the shift==0 branch returns true, and neither m_refusals++ nor the false that the shift>0 case gets is executed. Available() returns 1 for that single group (372), so an availability check does not protect a caller. Reachable: early in a bar-driven session (OnSessionStart zeroes m_count, the first pump publishes a handful of M1 bars), or right after session start where PrimeView clamps `from` to StartMsc (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:396-397), or after a deep OnRewind - any moment when the whole buffer fits inside one H1/H4/D1 group.

The control flow is as described. Group() walks newest-to-oldest; reaching line 136 with seen==0 means no bar from an earlier group was ever seen, i.e. the whole buffer lies inside group 0, so out.open is m_m1[0].open (the oldest buffered M1) rather than the group's true open, and the shift==0 early return at 138-139 skips both m_refusals++ and the refusal that shift>0 receives (140-141). out.spread is whatever line 110's `out = m_m1[i]` copied from the group's NEWEST M1 and is never aggregated. Available() returns 1 for groups==1 (line 372), so an availability check does not protect the caller. tick_volume/real_volume are correctly aggregated (no double count), so the defect is confined to open and spread.

The asymmetry is real and provable. When the backward walk exhausts the buffer while still inside group 0, the post-loop block at 132-138 returns true for shift 0 while shift>0 gets m_refusals++ and false, and out.open was last written at line 125 from m_m1[0] - the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold, not the group's first M1 bar. Available() returns 1 for that state (`groups == 1 ? 1 : 0`), so the group is advertised as usable. Impact keeps this LOW: the state needs the entire M1 buffer to lie inside one tf group, which in practice means the first minutes of a session or just after a jump+prime with few bars, and it only ever affects shift 0 - the bar this class already documents as unreliable and tells strategies not to act on. The shipped reference strategy is protected twice over (it requires Available(tf) >= lookback+2 and reads shifts 1 and 2), so nothing in the product observes it today.
strategy-integration-report-13.corrected: Same defect, two corrections. (1) The trigger is not merely "the group began before the buffer did" and it is not reachable via MakeRoom: MakeRoom keeps 2048 M1 bars (~34 hours), which always spans several H4 groups, so the early-return at line 104 fires first. It needs the entire buffer to lie inside the requested shift-0 group, which happens early in a session or just after a rewind that trimmed almost everything. (2) high and low are NOT right either - they are folded only over the minutes present in the buffer, so the group's true extreme can be in the missing earlier part. Only close is certainly correct. out.spread being the newest minute's value (copied once at line 110) is arguably the intended reading of a forming bar's spread rather than a defect.

What the user observes is worse than the finding states: because the frozen snapshot never changes, the `last.close > hi` test in CSSRRefBreakout::OnBar evaluates identically on every bar for the rest of the session, so the strategy either never signals again or re-enters the same stale breakout every time MyOpenCount() drops to zero, with a stop anchored to an hour-old range and a risk-derived lot sized off that distance. Available() keeps reporting the frozen group count, so no refusal counter or status line reveals it. HIGH stands: the layer whose stated purpose is that a strategy can only see published reality delivers a stale snapshot in the product's default fidelity, and virtual trades are placed on it.
strategy-integration-report-1.corrected: Accurate except for "no OnBarContext for the whole session": any pump owing >= SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC (10 minutes, e.g. after a real timer stall) degrades to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR in CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide and does take the bar-driven path, publishing bars and refreshing the view. reasons: Both halves check out against the source. CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks derives `now` solely from ticks[count-1] (184), computes bar_open from it (194) and can advance m_last_bar past several boundaries in one step (202-207), so any bar close that is not the last boundary in the batch is silently skipped - and OnTick likewise fires once per batch, not per tick. In FULL_TICK the batch is the whole window (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:366), so the number of boundaries inside one batch is bounded only by the pump ceiling. The wall-clock dependence is also provable: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2735 computes `delta` from GetMicrosecondCount() and feeds it to Pump, which reaches m_clock.Advance(wall_delta_ms) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1006), so window boundaries - and in the bar-driven path the ClipBar/tick-trim boundary at 459-470 - move with CPU load, which moves the tick on which OnBar fires and therefore the Bid/Ask the strategy reads and the price the engine fills at. Contrast confirmed: CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks iterates all ticks, so the account layer is batch-independent while the strategy layer is not. This breaks the explicit contract at SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24.

The mechanism is source-provable. The host reads only ticks[count-1] (184) and derives bar_open from it, so every earlier tick in the batch is invisible to the `bar_open > m_last_bar[i]` test (202-207) and m_last_bar jumps straight over any intermediate boundary; contrast CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks, which iterates all ticks, making the account batch-invariant. Batch size is a wall-clock artefact: Pump takes wall_delta_ms (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:996, whose own comment only promises determinism for 'identical delta sequences'), the FULL_TICK branch publishes the whole window in one PublishTicks (366), and in the bar-driven path the newest bar is ClipBar'd at wherever `hi` fell (159, 280-309), so the replay instant at which OnBar fires - and hence the ctx.market.Bid()/Ask() CSSRRefBreakout tests at RefStrategy:115 and the price the engine fills at - moves with pump boundaries.

The mechanism is confirmed. The host reads only ticks[count-1].time_msc (line 184) and derives bar_open from it, so every earlier tick in the batch is invisible to the bar-close test, and OnBar therefore fires at whatever replay instant the batch happens to end on. In the bar-driven path that instant is wall-clock dependent through clipping: the per-M1-bar segments are built from ClipBar against the pump's `hi` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:~455 and 506-507), so whether the first M1 bar of a new group arrives whole or clipped mid-minute - a function of the wall delta the clock scaled - moves the Bid()/Ask() the strategy sees at OnBar and hence the fill CSSRTradingEngine gives it and whether CSSRRefBreakout's `sl >= Bid()` gate trips. Downgraded from HIGH: nothing here corrupts money arithmetic or weakens the virtual-only guarantee - the account still prices every tick - the strategy layer is opt-in, and the per-run deviation is a few ticks of entry price. strategy-integration-report-2.corrected: The defect is real; the worked arithmetic is not. The probe at line 245 is CalendarValueHistory(probe, from, to) with NO country_code and NO currency argument — unlike Pull, which passes a currency (line 137) — and no importance filter, so it asks for every event of every country in the window. `from`/`to` are the caller's window widened by 86400 s at each end (lines 217-218), so the probe always spans at least ~2 full days plus the window; the 2024.12.25 example resolves to 2024.12.24..2024.12.26. The misleading note the finding describes therefore exists as a code path but has no reachable input on a terminal whose calendar is present. The suggested alternatives are a style preference, not a fix for a reachable defect.

strategy-integration-report-7.corrected: The mechanism is confirmed but the scenario is wrong: m_last_seq is advanced to each executed sequence (line 243), so after a restart the collision is not the third command but at most one command, and only when the incoming sequence exactly equals the last one executed. In the finding's own example (previous client reached seq 3, restarted client sends 1,2,3) nothing is dropped — 1 != 3 executes and sets m_last_seq to 1, then 2 and 3 follow normally. The reachable cases are: a restarted client whose first command is seq 1 while the publisher's last executed sequence happened to be 1 (the previous client had executed exactly one command), and two clients sharing one slot whose independent counters momentarily coincide. Full trace confirms the silent no-op, and it is worse than latent. m_warmup_to_msc is set by OnWarmupPlanned to m_timeline.start_msc-1 (Controller:814-816). I tried to refute this on three fronts and failed on all three.
