reasons: The arithmetic replays exactly and the defect reaches the product. In SSR_BarToTicks (SpikeKit:565-598) u = i*3/(cnt-1), so k[1] and k[2] are sampled only when some i makes u an integer, i.e. when (cnt-1)%3==0; the forced write at 594-597 fixes the close alone. For cnt=20 (B1:23 InpPerBar) the nearest samples to u=1 and u=2 are 0.9474/1.1053 and 1.8947/2.0526, giving the quoted ~5.3% shortfall on each extreme. Crucially CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-183) is the identical formula with m_ticks_per_bar defaulting to 8 (line 71) and InpTicksPerBar=8 in the shipping host (Standalone.mq5:75, 1148), where the step is 3/7 and the extremes are under-reached by 14.3% of the adjacent leg - contradicting the file header's "The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact" (line 11). The sl-tp-execution category is right, not a stretch: CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks feeds m_bid/m_ask per tick and CheckStops (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:513-544) compares only that tick price against sl/tp, so a stop sitting in the outer 14% of the O-to-extreme leg is never triggered even though BarIsAmbiguousFor considers the bar's real range.

I re-derived the arithmetic rather than trusting it, and it holds. u = i*3/(cnt-1) reaches the interior keypoints k[1] and k[2] exactly only when some i makes u == 1.0 and u == 2.0, i.e. when (cnt-1) % 3 == 0. cnt = MathMax(n,4) (SpikeKit:565). For B1's InpPerBar=20: cnt-1 = 19, nearest u values to 2.0 are 12*3/19 = 1.8947 (seg 1, f 0.8947) and 13*3/19 = 2.0526 (seg 2, f 0.0526), giving a peak of H - 0.0526*(H-C); nearest to 1.0 are 0.947 and 1.105, giving a trough of L + 0.0526*(O-L). On O=100/H=140/L=90/C=130 that is 139.47 and 90.53 - the 0.53 the finding states. The forced final write (SpikeKit:595-597) fixes only the close, and i = cnt-1 already lands on the close anyway (u=3 -> seg clamped to 2, f=1.0 -> p = k[3]). The load-bearing part is that the product shares the formula verbatim: CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:130-175) is the same u/seg/f interpolation with m_ticks_per_bar defaulting to 8 and the host input InpTicksPerBar = 8 (Standalone:75, 1148, 497). With n=8, cnt-1 = 7: the low is missed by 0.143*(O-L) and the high by 0.143*(H-C) - a 14.3% shortfall on every synthesised bar - while that file's own header line 12 states 'The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact'. No integer-division or array-bounds misreading is involved; the arithmetic is all double. Only cnt in {4,7,10,13,16,...} is exact. refuted=true records that I could not break it.
spikes-audits-1.corrected: Confirmed and broader than the title: the same defect is in the shipping engine (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-144) at its default 8 ticks/bar, where the shortfall is ~14.3% of the adjacent leg, and because CheckStops evaluates SL/TP off the tick price alone it silently misses stops placed near a bar's extreme. The spike kit is only where it was first written.

reasons: Every cited number verifies. GroupPort:354-356 admits pendings into the row array while GroupPort:240 sets out.open_positions = m_acct.OpenCount(), which counts only SSR_POS_OPEN (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:974-980; a separate PendingCount() exists at 981 and is unused here). out.pending_count is incremented at GroupPort:372 and grep over MQL5/ finds it nowhere else except its declaration (SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:124) and its clear (261) - no consumer. SSR_Panel.mqh:1513 computes shown from pos_rows while 1640-1642 gates the "+N more" line on open_positions > shown and prints open_positions - shown. PosCap() = (134-22)/(SSR_ROW_H+1) with SSR_ROW_H=19 (SSR_Theme.mqh:511) = 5 on the normal panel. So 2 opens + 4 pendings gives pos_rows 6, shown 5, open_positions 2, 2 > 5 false - one row vanishes with no indicator, and since the fill loop runs newest-first (GroupPort:340) the casualty is the oldest order, exactly the "order you forget you left there" the comment at 346-353 exists to prevent.

Every number in the claim checks out against the files. GroupPort's row loop admits both states (bool pend = (vp.state == SSR_POS_PENDING); if(vp.state != SSR_POS_OPEN && !pend) continue; at l.354-356) and increments the shared pos_rows for each (l.358), while out.open_positions = m_acct.OpenCount() (l.240) counts only SSR_POS_OPEN - confirmed at TradingEngine:974-980, with a separate PendingCount() at 981-987 that the port never calls. pending_count is written at GroupPort:372 and nowhere read: the only other occurrences in the whole tree are its declaration (ReplayPort:124) and its clear (ReplayPort:261). The panel's indicator compares the two mismatched quantities: shown = min(pos_rows, cap) (Panel:1513) against if(m_state.open_positions > shown) ... open_positions - shown (Panel:1637-1642). PosCap() = (PosGroupH() - 22) / (SSR_ROW_H + 1) with PosGroupH() = 134 non-tall (Panel:443) and SSR_ROW_H = 19 (Theme:511), so cap = 112/20 = 5 exactly as claimed. Scenario 1 (2 open + 4 pending): pos_rows 6, shown 5, open_positions 2, so 2 > 5 is false, no 'not shown' text is drawn, and the oldest row - reachable as a pending, since the loop walks newest-first - is simply absent. Scenario 2 (20 open + 4 pending): pos_rows saturates at SSR_POS_MAX = 12 (ReplayPort:29), shown 5, and the line reports 20-5 = '15 not shown' while 19 of the 24 live items are off the sheet. This is precisely the failure the 'PENDING ORDERS ARE ROWS TOO / an order you cannot see is an order you forget you left there' comment at GroupPort:346-353 exists to prevent. refuted=true records that I could not break it.
ui-port-session-9.corrected: Confirmed; one arithmetic nit in the second scenario: pos_rows is capped at SSR_POS_MAX=12 (SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:29, loop guard at GroupPort:340), so with 20 opens + 4 pendings only 12 rows are ever collected - the line still misreports ("15 not shown" against 19 items actually absent), but 12 rows, not 24, exist to hide.

reasons: Trace confirms no cache and no header-only mode anywhere on the path. SessionSummary (GroupPort:932-940) calls m_sessions.Peek, which constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)) (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:215-219); Load (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-259) reads the file line by line to EOF, growing m_ent_sec/m_ent_key/m_ent_val for every entry - pos, leg and e rows included - before Peek reads its five keys. The dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) inside the row loop for SSR_SD_ROWS=8 (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:27, 157-178), and Render() runs from Open() and from the up, down, row, load and del handlers (255, 257, 262-268, 284, 293). Severity stays LOW: it is a modal, user-paced interaction and the cost is a file parse per visible row per click, not a correctness fault.

Mechanism verified end to end. CSSRSessionManager::Peek (SessionManager:216-243) constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)); Load (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-259) reads the file line by line to EOF, appending every key=value pair - including every pos/leg/e row - into the dynamic m_ent_sec/m_ent_key/m_ent_val arrays before Peek reads its five [session] keys. GroupPort::SessionSummary (l.932-940) calls Peek per index with no cache, and the dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) inside its row loop bounded by SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SessionDialog:27, 172-173), with Render() re-entered on up, down, row click, load and after save (SessionDialog:255-257, 264, 284, and Open() from RequestSave). There is no header-only read mode anywhere. Two corrections to the magnitude rather than the mechanism: the parse is bounded by SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 and SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS = 1024 (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:33-34), so the worst case is ~16k entries per file and ~131k per render, not the unbounded 9,000-per-file figure implied; and the cost is string/array work in a modal that a human clicks a handful of times, so it is an efficiency wart, not a hang. Severity stays LOW.
ui-port-session-12.corrected: Accurate: Peek fully parses each session file and the dialog calls it once per visible row on every Render(), with no cache and no header-only mode. The per-file parse is capped by SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 / SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS = 1024, so the worst case is roughly 8 x 16k entries per click rather than an unbounded amount.

The data defect is provable. GroupPort::SaveSession (l.942-957) does SSRSessionSettings set; set.Init(); then overwrites only set.slot, and Init() (SessionManager:62-67) hardcodes seed 0, blind 0, pause_flags 0, session_mode 0, ticks_per_bar 8, spread_points 0.0, chart_tf PERIOD_M5. The host path does it correctly (CollectSettings at Standalone:415, called at 2138), so two saves of the same live session disagree by which button produced them, and SaveSession is reachable from the dialog at SessionDialog:242 and 318. reasons: The truncation is plainly in the source. SSRFlightSample.chart_id is a long (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:58), filled from g_charts.IdAt(0) at Standalone.mq5:2408-2409, and Write formats it as (int)s.chart_id against a %d specifier (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:243, 256), so any id above 2^31-1 is written wrapped and often negative into the chart_id column of the diagnostic artefact. The finding is honest that "real chart ids exceed 2^31" is an inference about MT5's id scheme rather than evidence from this tree - but the cast is lossy for such ids regardless, and the fix (%I64d or IntegerToString) needs no runtime knowledge. The same (int) cast is applied to emit_calls/emit_ticks/seed_bars/truncations at 254-255.

The cast is real and lossy: FlightRecorder:256 passes (int)s.chart_id into a %d slot of the sample row, and s.chart_id is filled from g_charts.IdAt(0), a long chart id (Standalone:2407-2409). MQL5's StringFormat %d takes a 32-bit argument, so a long id has to be widened to %I64d or routed through IntegerToString rather than truncated; C-style truncation of a value above 2^31 yields a wrong and frequently negative number in the one column that says which window a fault occurred on, in the artefact the author depends on for remote diagnosis. The one thing I cannot settle from this tree is the magnitude of real MT5 chart ids - that comes from MT5's time-derived id scheme, not from source - but the cast is unconditionally lossy above 2^31 whatever the distribution, and no other code in the tree ever narrows a chart id this way. I do refute the extension of the claim to the instrumentation counters: (int)s.emit_ticks and (int)s.emit_calls would need 2^31 ticks in one recording (at 8 ticks per bar that is ~268M bars), which SSR_FLIGHT_MAX_ROWS-capped sessions cannot plausibly reach, so those casts are not a live defect. Severity LOW: a diagnostic column, not behaviour.
chart-13.corrected: Confirmed for chart_id. The emit_ticks/emit_calls half is far weaker: those would need to exceed 2.1 billion in one recording (over 268 million bars at the default 8 ticks/bar) before wrapping, so in practice chart_id is the only column that truncates.
